solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Killjoy is mean to exclude student

indicators.note: to exclude tells us to leave the student's letter out of the word for mean

parts.note: mean in the sense of stingy is miserly
L is the learner plate letter, a student driver

explanation.surface: A spoilsport is described as stingy enough to shut a pupil out.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserable spoilsport is called a misery in informal speech, a synonym for a killjoy.

clue.text: Native Americans rejected order by those in favour of war

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the order's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
hawks are those who advocate military action

explanation.surface: Indigenous people refused an instruction from warmongers.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit; 'order' looks like a command.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are an Iroquois people of North America, so the plural names members of that nation.

clue.text: Restrictions in reporting scuppered cuts

indicators.note: in reporting means as it would be spoken, so the two words are said out loud

parts.note: a scuppered ship sank, and to cut someone dead is to shun them; the pair spoken together

explanation.surface: News coverage mentions limits that were wrecked by spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuppered cuts' must be read as two verbs, past and present, not adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctions are penalties or embargoes that restrict a country's trade or conduct.

clue.text: Referee chooses rounds to repeat again

indicators.note: rounds means surrounds, so the two words wrap the letters wanted

explanation.surface: An umpire selects bouts to replay.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing a second time is reverberating once more, so to resound repeatedly.

clue.text: Greek expert on the underworld put to shame

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the Greek expert after the underworld

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A scholar of Hades in Greek myth, perhaps, is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman name for the underworld and its god. In an across clue 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgrace someone is to shame them publicly, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: British Island briefly joins American state

parts.note: IOW is the short form of the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An English island, in short, joins a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England, abbreviated IOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the US, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Steps taken quickly upset doctor, and cause suffering and delay

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the joined pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
lag means delay

explanation.surface: An unhurried physician is distressed and procrastinates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses DRAILLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The galliard is a lively Renaissance court dance with quick leaping steps.

clue.text: Special language discovered by thieves originally

definitions.text: Special language discovered by thieves originally

indicators.note: discovered here means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: jargon is the special vocabulary of a trade or group

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word for robbers

explanation.surface: A secret tongue was first devised by criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the covering letters from JARGON, leaving ARGO; the whole clue also describes the word's origin as thieves' cant.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the slang of a particular group, and the term began in French as criminals' cant.

clue.text: Went on stage last, captivating theatre after removing hat

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the final word encloses the rest

parts.note: the last part is the end

indicators.note: the letters of hat are taken out of theatre, one by one in order

explanation.surface: An actor made a late appearance, enthralling the playhouse once the headgear came off.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat comes off letter by letter, not as one block, and 'captivating' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who comes on stage has entered, the stage direction for arriving.

clue.text: Someone who seeks to relinquish one extreme for another in tasting desire

indicators.text: to relinquish one extreme for another in tasting
indicators.note: the word tasting has two ends, T and G; the seeker gives up the first of them in favour of the other

parts.note: a hunter is someone who seeks game or treasure

explanation.surface: A seeker swaps one extreme for another while sampling food, out of craving.
explanation.walkthrough: The two extremes are the end letters of 'tasting': its T is dropped from the seeker and its G put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger is a strong craving or longing, a noun synonym for desire.

clue.text: Mainly get Kindle when it's hard to see clearly

definitions.text: when it's hard to see clearly

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to twig is to get, understand
to kindle a fire is to light it

explanation.surface: Mostly, reading on a Kindle e-reader is done when vision is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle, the e-reader brand, is just the verb 'set alight' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, the dim period after sunset, is the time when visibility is poor.

clue.text: Return to old ways is concerning liberal part of Church

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Going back to tradition involves the progressive wing of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal part of Church' suggests a faction, but it splits into L and APSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slide back into former bad habits, a noun sense of backsliding.

clue.text: Guards cycling contest with revolutionary new screen

indicators.note: to screen is to shield, so the turned word wraps around the other piece
revolutionary means turned round, so new is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the contest word round to its end

parts.note: a match is a contest

explanation.surface: A bike race is shown with a radical new display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' turns MATCH into ATCHM; 'revolutionary' turns NEW into WEN, which screens it.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchmen are sentries or night guards, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Season with continental football team …

parts.note: Inter is Inter Milan, an Italian club side

explanation.surface: A sports term is played alongside a European side, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, whose 'this' points back here.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Regularly adopt fashionable clothes all over the place

indicators.note: clothes means dresses, so the stylish word wraps around the picked letters

parts.note: chic means stylish

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of adopt

explanation.surface: Routinely wearing trendy outfits, scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes A, O, T from 'adopt'; 'clothes' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is disordered and messy, the same idea as all over the place.

clue.text: … succeeded immediately, producing this

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
now means immediately

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the season followed at once, bringing what winter brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers back to the previous clue's answer: winter produces snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen flakes are what the cold season brings, so the pointer word stands for them.

clue.text: Miles pens article to secure ancestral home

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the word for distant holds the article

parts.note: something miles away is far
the is the definite article
to land a deal is to secure it

explanation.surface: A man named Miles writes a piece to buy his family's old house.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles reads as a name but stands for distance.
explanation.definitionFit: One's fatherland is the native country of one's forebears.

clue.text: From the outset Britons inhabiting Australian region displaced her?

definitions.text: From the outset Britons inhabiting Australian region displaced her?

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged
from the outset takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: From the start, British settlers moving into an Australian area pushed out the original inhabitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges BIA with REGION; the whole clue also describes colonial settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indigenous Australian, one of the people dispossessed by British settlers from the outset of colonisation.

clue.text: He saves judge coming between heads of state meeting face to face

indicators.note: coming between means placed inside the pair of monarchs
two monarchs face each other, so the first one is turned round to look at the second

parts.note: ER is the monarch, Elizabeth Regina
a second ER, another monarch
to deem is to judge

explanation.surface: A rescuer arbitrates between two leaders at a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard monarch; two facing each other means the first is turned round, and 'coming between' puts the judge inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is called the Saviour; one who rescues or ransoms others is their deliverer.

clue.text: State requiring spiritual and political liberation?

definitions.text: State requiring spiritual and political liberation?

parts.words: State requiring spiritual and political liberation?
parts.note: being taken over by a demon needs spiritual deliverance by exorcism, while a colony or dependent territory seeks political liberation

explanation.surface: A nation needing freedom both of soul and of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' works twice: a condition of the soul, and a territory ruled by another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonic occupation is a spiritual condition, and a dependent territory ruled from abroad is a political holding.

clue.text: Food and drink containing energy

indicators.note: containing means the aperitif holds the energy letter

parts.note: pastis is an anise-flavoured French aperitif
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Meals and beverages provide calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food and drink' reads as a pair, but 'Food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasties are savoury baked pastry turnovers, a kind of food.

clue.text: In an institution for people who need help

definitions.meaning: being in means being at your house rather than out

definitions.text: institution for people who need help
definitions.meaning: a care establishment for the elderly or needy

explanation.surface: Living inside a care facility for the vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at their dwelling is in; a residential care centre is a familiar name for such an institution.

clue.text: Promote side almost winning final in extra time

indicators.note: winning means gaining, so the shortened team takes in the other letters
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players

indicators.note: the final letter of extra

explanation.surface: A team nearly victorious in a cup final during extra time earns promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ELEVEN to ELEVE; 'winning' puts A and T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise them in rank, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Make good theatre company start to understudy parts

indicators.note: parts means splits, so the theatre word is opened to take the other letters

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drama troupe compensates by beginning to hire stand-ins for roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre company' reads as one noun but gives two pieces, and 'parts' is a verb meaning splits, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup a loss is to recover or compensate for it, the same idea as making good.

clue.text: Pit worker's person who likes to be high

definitions.meaning: someone who removes stones, or pits, from fruit, not a miner

definitions.text: person who likes to be high
definitions.meaning: slang for a habitual cannabis user

explanation.surface: A coal miner is said to enjoy getting high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit worker' suggests a miner, but the pits are fruit stones; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit-pitting device or person, and slang for a regular cannabis smoker.

clue.text: Violent attack supported by firm

parts.note: on means resting upon, supported by
set means firm or fixed

explanation.surface: A brutal assault is backed by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it means solid.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or onslaught, an old military sense.

clue.text: Electronic issue containing nothing about graphic history

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
containing places zero inside the joined electronic issue

parts.note: to emit is to issue
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: An e-book edition with nothing on illustrated history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' builds ENILEMIT, which 'about' then turns end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronological chart is a visual account of events, a historical diagram.

clue.text: Five stopping to help up drama queen

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the numeral sits inside
up in a down clue means read upwards, so the helping word is backwards

parts.note: aid means to help
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five people stop to lift up a theatrical attention-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AID to DIA, and 'stopping' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental, self-important person is called a prima donna, a synonym for a drama queen.

clue.text: It's always Sleepless in Seattle's opening I moan about

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
about signals the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble about the romantic film Sleepless in Seattle and its start.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepless in Seattle is a 1990s romcom; 'about' rearranges I MOAN to OMNIA after IN and the S from 'opening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic inability to sleep is the condition of being forever wakeful.

clue.text: Kinky cross-dresser procures sex for nymphette

indicators.note: procures means gets hold of, so the Kinks character takes in the coy word

parts.note: Lola is the cross-dressing subject of the Kinks' song Lola
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A deviant transvestite pays for intercourse with a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' refers to the band the Kinks, whose 1970 hit Lola concerns a cross-dresser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's novel title character, a seductive young girl, became a byword for one.

clue.text: Study leads to academics rebutting arguments separately within 24-hour period

indicators.note: separately signals that the letters are split apart and reassembled
the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Revision makes scholars counter debating points one by one over a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter slots A, R, A one at a time into STUDY ('separately within'); the parse shows it as a rearrangement of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth day of the week is one particular day, a specific twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Without children present, you have a ball!

parts.note: SP stands for the Latin sine prole, without offspring, used in genealogies
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: With no kids around, you can have a great time.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the genealogists' abbreviation for sine prole, 'without issue'; 'ball' is a globe, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe or orb is a round solid, just like a ball.
